competitions.name: AssetOpsBench
competitions.tagline: Benchmark LLM agents on multi-step industrial asset operations and maintenance scenarios scored by an LLM judge.
competitions.description: AssetOpsBench is an IBM Research benchmark of 141+ industrial asset-operations scenarios spanning IoT telemetry, failure-mode/sensor relations, time-series forecasting, work orders, and vibration diagnostics, exposed through six MCP servers. Agents (plan-execute, Claude, OpenAI, Deep, OpenCode, Stirrup, direct-LLM) are run against each scenario and their trajectories are scored by an LLM judge (Llama-4-Maverick-17B) on a 6-dimensional rubric covering reasoning, execution, and data handling. It has powered public competitions (CODS 2025 AssetOpsBench-Live, IJCAI 2026 Industrial Automation Challenge) and is accepted at KDD 2026. It matters because it gives a reproducible, tool-grounded testbed for evaluating agentic AI in Industry 4.0 settings.

participation.howToSubmit: Contribute new scenarios via a Pull Request or an Issue tagged `new-scenario`; run the benchmark with the scenario-suite runner and submit agent trajectories for evaluation. Competition submissions go through the external challenge sites (Codabench for CODS 2025, the IJCAI 2026 challenge site).
participation.submissionFormat: Scenario definitions following the Utterance and Ground Truth design guidelines, plus agent trajectory JSON files evaluated by the offline `uv run evaluate` CLI.
participation.computeDetails: Agents call LLM APIs (LiteLLM proxy / TokenRouter); MCP servers run locally with CouchDB in Docker. No GPU requirement stated.
participation.rounds: Competitions run as separate events (CODS 2025 completed; IJCAI 2026 live)
participation.eligibility: Open to researchers, students, and practitioners worldwide
participation.verification: Offline evaluation module scores saved trajectories with registered graders (llm_judge 6-criterion rubric, static_json); competition entries verified on external platforms.
requirements: MCP servers (iot, fmsr, tsfm, wo, vibration, utilities)

venue.event: KDD 2026 (Jeju, South Korea); IJCAI 2026 competition; CODS 2025

competitions.quickstart:
git clone https://github.com/IBM/AssetOpsBench.git
cd AssetOpsBench
pip install -e .
# or with uv:
uv sync
cp .env.public .env
python -m assetopsbench.run --scenario "List all sensors of Chiller 6 in MAIN site"

competitions.name: AlpacaEval
competitions.tagline: Automatic LLM-as-judge benchmark measuring instruction-following win rate against a reference model.
competitions.description: AlpacaEval evaluates instruction-following chat models by having a strong LLM annotator (e.g. GPT-4-turbo) compare a model's outputs against a reference model's outputs on the 805-example AlpacaEval set, reporting win rate and length-controlled win rate. It is fast (<5 min) and cheap (<$10) and correlates 0.98 with ChatBot Arena. Maintained by the tatsu-lab (Stanford) team; anyone can submit a model via a pull request adding a model config, outputs, and a leaderboard entry.

participation.howToSubmit: Fork the repo, add a model config under src/alpaca_eval/models_configs/<model_name>, run `alpaca_eval evaluate_from_model --model_configs '<model_name>'`, then open a PR adding the config, outputs, and updated leaderboard entry.
participation.submissionFormat: Model config YAML, model_outputs.json, annotations.json, and updated leaderboard CSV under src/alpaca_eval/leaderboards/
participation.computeDetails: GPU needed only for local HuggingFace model decoding; annotation is done via API (e.g. OpenAI).
participation.eligibility: Open to anyone; top-5 models can request verification by maintainers.
participation.cost: free (plus annotator API costs, <$10 per run)
participation.verification: Community submissions via PR; top-5 models can be verified by a core maintainer who re-decodes and re-evaluates.
requirements: OpenAI API key (or other annotator provider)

competitions.name: VBench
competitions.tagline: Benchmark and leaderboard for video generative models across quality, semantic, and faithfulness dimensions.
competitions.description: VBench is a comprehensive benchmark suite for video generative models, decomposing video generation quality into hierarchical evaluation dimensions with dedicated prompt suites and automatic evaluation methods. Models are scored per dimension, then aggregated into Quality, Semantic, and Total scores (VBench), I2V and Quality scores (VBench-I2V), or Creativity/Commonsense/Controllability/Human Fidelity/Physics scores (VBench-2.0). It is maintained by the Vchitect team and hosted on Hugging Face, with submissions accepted via evaluation result JSON files.

participation.howToSubmit: Run the evaluation scripts locally, pack the evaluation_results directory into a zip, optionally compute the final score with scripts/cal_final_score.py, then submit the JSON to the Hugging Face leaderboard space.
participation.submissionFormat: evaluation_results.zip containing per-dimension JSON results; optionally a computed total score JSON.
participation.computeDetails: Evaluation requires GPU (CUDA) for feature extractors such as DINO, RAFT, UMT, ViCLIP; VBench-2.0 recommends up to 8 GPUs for parallel dimension evaluation.
participation.eligibility: Open to all video generative model developers and researchers.
participation.verification: Automatic evaluation scripts and leaderboard submission review; results are reproducible via provided code.

competitions.quickstart:
pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu118
pip install vbench
vbench evaluate --videos_path $VIDEO_PATH --dimension $DIMENSION
cd evaluation_results && zip -r ../evaluation_results.zip .
python scripts/cal_final_score.py --zip_file evaluation_results.zip --model_name your_model_name

competitions.tagline: Agents solve 75 Kaggle ML engineering competitions; scored by percentage of medals won within a time budget.
competitions.description: MLE-bench evaluates AI agents on 75 Kaggle competitions, measuring the percentage of competitions where the agent's submission earns a medal (Any Medal %). participation.rounds: Continuous leaderboard; submissions currently paused (as of 2026-04-24) while a new fairness process is developed.
participation.eligibility: Open to any team or individual; agents must not use test-set labels.
participation.verification: Grading reports reviewed by maintainers; rule violation and plagiarism detectors available; test-set feedback submissions flagged separately.

competitions.name: ClawProBench
competitions.tagline: Benchmark LLM agents on real OpenClaw runtime tasks, ranked by stable repeated success (FinalScore).
competitions.description: ClawProBench is a live-first benchmark harness that evaluates model capability inside the OpenClaw agent runtime across 102 active scenarios in 6 domains, with deterministic grading and structured reports. Models are run with --trials 3 and ranked by FinalScore = 100 × S^0.40 × r_all^0.45 × r_any^0.15, where S is average_score, r_all = (pass^3)^(1/3) and r_any = 1 - (1 - pass@3)^(1/3). It is maintained by YuanHang Xiao (suyoumo) with a public leaderboard, an arXiv paper, and a Hugging Face dataset; results are published for frontier and preview models, and third-party API providers can request evaluation of their served models.

participation.howToSubmit: Run the harness locally against a model and contact xyh920691910@outlook.com to submit results or discuss evaluation for the leaderboard; third-party API gateway providers can request that their served models be benchmarked and published.
participation.submissionFormat: Benchmark reports written to results/ by run.py (avg_score, max_score, pass^3, pass@3, coverage-aware summaries, cost, latency, resume metadata).
participation.computeDetails: Runs the local OpenClaw runtime; cost depends on the model API used. Multi-trial runs (--trials 3) are the default ranking path.
participation.rounds: Continuous leaderboard updates; open-source dataset and closed-dataset leaderboards run in parallel.
participation.eligibility: Open to model providers and third-party API gateway providers; contact the maintainer to have models evaluated and published.
participation.verification: Deterministic grading via scenario-specific custom checkers in custom_checks/, with live OpenClaw execution and structured reports.

python3 run.py compare --results-dir results

competitions.name: Polymarket Paper Trader — Forecast Arena & AI Trader Leaderboard
competitions.tagline: Forecast real Polymarket questions or paper-trade them; scored by Brier score and ROI against the crowd.
competitions.description: A zero-risk gym and benchmark for AI agents on real Polymarket prediction markets. The Forecast Arena has AI models and naive baselines publish one YES probability per soon-resolving binary market before it resolves, scored by Brier score, ECE and alpha vs the crowd; the AI Trader Leaderboard ranks agents by ROI% on a $10k paper account with real order books and official fees. Both are run by the agent-next project, with the arena board published at polymarket-leaderboard.com and entries submitted via PR/issue or the arena workflow.

participation.howToSubmit: Forecast Arena: add your entrant to arena.yaml and open a PR (or run the arena workflow). AI Trader Leaderboard: generate a leaderboard entry with `leaderboard_entry` (MCP) or `pm-trader leaderboard` (CLI) and open an issue titled `[SUBMIT] {agent_name} — ROI: {roi}%` with the JSON body.
participation.submissionFormat: arena.yaml entrant entry (id, label, kind, model, disclosure metadata) for the arena; JSON stats output from `leaderboard_entry` pasted into a GitHub issue for the trading leaderboard.
participation.computeDetails: Forecasting and paper trading are API/CPU-bound; no GPU required.
participation.rounds: Daily arena runs; trading leaderboard is continuous.
participation.verification: Arena forecasts are recorded append-only before resolution and scored against real outcomes; trading entries are self-reported JSON stats reviewed by maintainers.
requirements: litellm-compatible model API key (for AI entrants)

competitions.name: GPU MODE Kernel Leaderboards

competitions.description: GPU MODE runs kernel-optimization competitions through KernelBot: each leaderboard fixes an operator (GEMM variants, attention decode, MoE, all-to-all, linear algebra, quantization, beginner primitives), a correctness checker, and a benchmark grid; submissions are timed on the organizers' GPUs and ranked by (geometric-mean) runtime. 42 leaderboards, 3178 ranked entries from 1605 users on B200, A100, B200_Nebius, MI355X, NVIDIA, MI300x8, H100, L4, MI300, T4; 8 currently accept submissions. Reference problems and evaluators live in gpu-mode/reference-kernels.

Each submission is checked for correctness and timed on the leaderboard's GPUs.

participation.computeDetails: Benchmarks run on GPU MODE's hardware (A100, H100, B200, L4, T4, MI300, MI300x8, MI355X); no local GPU is required, though one helps for iteration.
participation.deadline: per leaderboard; beginner v2 problems are open-ended
participation.prizes: varies by competition (sponsored rounds have prizes)
participation.eligibility: Open to everyone with an account.
participation.verification: Server-side correctness checks and timing; top submissions are re-validated against a stricter contract on some leaderboards.

competitions.name: JevBench
competitions.tagline: Benchmark for AI decision models: typed decision accuracy, calibration, latency and cost.
competitions.description: JevBench by Benchmark Heaven evaluates AI decision models and Jev-compatible systems on typed decisions: a state, a rubric and a bounded label set, answered with one typed answer and a probability. Systems are scored on Intelligence (chance-corrected accuracy), Calibration, Speed and Cost, combined into a JevBench Score (geometric mean, 25% each, with a near-chance penalty). It is maintained by Benchmark Heaven independently of TypeSafe AI; the canonical board is at benchmarkheaven.com/jev-models. Entrants are measured by the organizers through each author's published interface, and new systems are added on request.

participation.howToSubmit: Request a run by opening an issue (e.g. issue #6, #9) or replying to the launch posts; the organizers run your system through its author's published interface and add a row. Mappings, endpoint conditions and cost bases are pre-registered in docs/ before the run.
participation.submissionFormat: A reachable endpoint or public weights plus serving code; the organizers supply the adapter. Pre-registration documents the mapping and cost basis.
participation.computeDetails: Organizers run entrants on their own CPU, rented RunPod/lium.io GPUs (RTX 3090, A6000, RTX PRO 4500, A40, H100, H200) or the entrant's production API.
participation.rounds: Versioned releases (v1.0, v1.1, v1.1.3, v1.2.x, v1.3.0, v1.4.x, v1.5, v1.6.1); new systems are added as revisions on the same frozen items.
participation.verification: Organizers run the frozen task set serially through the entrant's own interface; scoring code is public (jevbench/composite_v13.py, composite_v14.py) and artifacts are rebuilt from frozen measurements.
requirements: A reachable HTTP endpoint or public weights

competitions.name: SqueezeBench
competitions.tagline: Prove Lean-verified lower or upper bounds on extremal combinatorics functions to squeeze f between records.
competitions.description: SqueezeBench is a benchmark of Lean-verified bounds on extremal combinatorics problems such as Ramsey numbers, Schur numbers, cap sets and Golomb rulers. Each problem has a lower and an upper track; a submission is a Lean function ℕ → ℕ with machine-checked proofs of valid, improves and strict, judged by Comparator against a frozen statement and checked by two independent kernels (Lean and nanoda). Records only ever improve, and the full credit is in each problem's record history.

participation.howToSubmit: Fork the repo, run `lake exe squeeze new <Problem> <lower|upper>` to lay out the next version, fill in Def.lean, Proof.lean, REPORT.md and metadata.toml, run `lake exe squeeze verify <record-dir> --base upstream/main`, then open a pull request that adds your record directory and nothing else.
participation.submissionFormat: One new directory under SqueezeBench/Problems/<Problem>/Records/<Lower|Upper>/V<k>/ containing Def.lean, Proof.lean, REPORT.md and metadata.toml.
participation.computeDetails: No GPU; verification is CPU-bound. `squeeze verify`'s fuel check alone peaks near 7 GB, and the Comparator runs in its own unit with a 16 GB limit.
participation.eligibility: Open to anyone; submissions are pull requests to the public repository.
participation.verification: Comparator against a statement frozen for that version, with every proof checked by two independent kernels: Lean's own and nanoda (Rust). No `sorry`, no new axioms, no `native_decide`.

organizer.name: Pablo Manrique, Hai Xia, Stefan Szeider (SqueezeBench team)

competitions.quickstart:
gh repo fork leansolving/SqueezeBench --clone
cd SqueezeBench
lake exe cache get
lake build
lake exe squeeze bootstrap
lake exe squeeze new <Problem> <lower|upper>
lake exe squeeze verify <record-dir> --base upstream/main

competitions.name: LeanEval
competitions.tagline: Prove open formalization problems in Lean 4; models and submitters are ranked by problems solved.
competitions.description: LeanEval is the Lean FRO's comparator-based benchmark for formal mathematics. Trusted theorem statements live in leanprover/lean-eval; a problem counts as solved when the comparator accepts a submitted proof. Results are sticky per (user, model, problem) and published at lean-lang.org/eval. 304 visible problems, 78 models, 62 submitters, 36 active problems still unsolved.

participation.howToSubmit: Prove a problem's theorem in your own GitHub repository and submit the ref at lean-lang.org/eval/submit; the comparator verifies the proof and the result is appended to results/<login>.json in leanprover/lean-eval-submissions.
participation.submissionFormat: GitHub repo + ref containing the completed Lean proof, plus the declared model label used to produce it.
participation.computeDetails: Scoring is a comparator check of the proof; whatever compute the prover needs is on the submitter's side.
participation.eligibility: Open to everyone. Successes are sticky: an accepted (user, model, problem) tuple is never removed.
participation.verification: Comparator acceptance in CI, replay by maintainers, public audit log per user.

competitions.quickstart:
git clone https://github.com/leanprover/lean-eval && cd lean-eval
lake exe cache get && lake build
lake exe lean-eval --help   # pick a problem under generated/, replace sorry, submit at lean-lang.org/eval/submit

competitions.name: ProgramBench
competitions.tagline: Score AI coding agents on real-world program-repair tasks; maximize mean per-instance score.
competitions.description: ProgramBench evaluates AI models and agent harnesses on a suite of software-engineering instances, scoring each instance by test pass rate. Submissions are registered as PRs to this registry repo, each contributing a folder with a pointer.yaml, submission.yaml manifest, and per-instance _stats JSON files. The public leaderboard at programbench.com is compiled directly from merged entries, and submissions are verified in two tiers (Tier-0 recomputes the headline; Tier-1 re-runs the full evaluation).

participation.howToSubmit: Open a PR to main adding a folder submissions/<submission_id>/ containing pointer.yaml, submission.yaml, and _stats/ (score.json required; cost.json and calls.json optional). Use `programbench submit register <your-run-dir>` to open the PR automatically.
participation.submissionFormat: submissions/<submission_id>/ with pointer.yaml (fork URL + pinned commit SHA), submission.yaml (model, provider, score headline), and _stats/score.json (flat {instance_id: value} map).
participation.computeDetails: Tier-0 verification requires no Docker; Tier-1 re-runs `programbench eval` on each submission.tar.gz.
participation.verification: Tier-0: `uvx programbench submit verify .` recomputes headline from eval.json and checks against submission.yaml. Tier-1: `uvx programbench submit verify . --tier1` re-runs evaluation and confirms fresh scores match.

competitions.quickstart:
git clone <a-public-submission-fork> && cd <fork>
uvx programbench submit verify .            # Tier-0: recompute headline vs manifest. No Docker.
uvx programbench submit verify . --tier1    # Tier-1: re-run eval and confirm the artifacts reproduce it.

participation.verification: Proofs are compiled and run in HOL Light; verdicts recorded as OK, FAIL, CHEATING, or ERROR.

competitions.name: Agent Anvil Public Leaderboard
competitions.tagline: Score agent tool-use safety with trace-aware assertions instead of final-answer-only checks.
competitions.description: Agent Anvil is a compact offline benchmark that compares final-answer-only grading with trace-aware assertions across tool-use safety scenarios. Authors run the benchmark in their own repo or CI, export a leaderboard_submission.json, and open a PR to this repository, where CI validates provenance and rebuilds the aggregate index. Rows are labeled self_reported, github_actions (with verified run URL and artifact attestation), or maintainer_rerun. The headline metric is trace-aware pass rate, which exposes policy violations that answer-only checks miss.

participation.howToSubmit: Run the benchmark in your repo, export leaderboard_submission.json with `anvil leaderboard export`, validate it, copy it to submissions/<agent-name>.json, and open a PR to main.
participation.submissionFormat: One JSON file per agent under submissions/ following schema agent-anvil.leaderboard.v1 (submitter, benchmark, metrics, artifacts, verification).
participation.computeDetails: Compact offline benchmark of 5 scenarios / 100 trials; no GPU required.
participation.eligibility: Open to any agent author; submissions via public PR.
participation.verification: CI validates the JSON, verifies GitHub run URLs via the GitHub API, checks artifact attestations for github_actions rows, and runs a leaderboard audit (accept/review/reject). Maintainer reruns are stored separately.

  --repo-url "https://github.com/acme/my-agent" \
  --commit-sha "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"

competitions.name: Apex Humanoid Parkour
competitions.tagline: Train an ONNX policy that walks a Unitree G1 through a 51 m parkour course under randomized friction and wind.
competitions.description: Miners submit an ONNX policy (<=15 MB, architecture free) that drives a 12-DoF Unitree G1 humanoid through a 51.1 m linear parkour course: on-ramp, drop, stairs, a 1 m leap, hurdle, step-up, duck-under, balance beam, slick patch and stairway down. Each round evaluates 24 instances of up to 3000 control steps with friction and wind drawn from an unpublished per-round seed, so open-loop trajectory replay is worthless. Scoring is progress-based: completions score in (1.0, 2.0] with a speed bonus, non-completions score their fraction of course covered, and raw_score is the mean over 24 instances. Run by Macrocosm (Apex competition, Bittensor Subnet 1); the reference Unitree stock walker reaches only 21% of the course.

participation.howToSubmit: Submit an ONNX policy graph through the Apex platform (Bittensor Subnet 1); the referee runs it in the player sandbox against 24 randomized instances.
participation.submissionFormat: ONNX graph, <= 15 MB, float32, interface obs[104] + state_in[256] -> action[12] + state_out[256]; architecture free (recurrent nets, ensembles, transformers over a history window).
participation.computeDetails: Referee runs under --cpus 1 --memory 1.5g; inference runs once per control step up to 72,000 times per evaluation, with a 900 s referee timeout. Training a policy is the miner's own responsibility.
participation.rounds: Rounds with per-round seeds; conditions (friction, wind) drawn per round and not published while the round is open.
participation.verification: Referee container runs the policy in a player sandbox; physics_glitch/invalid/player errors score 0.0; history and API log artifacts are collected per submission.

competitions.quickstart:
docker build -f referee/Dockerfile -t hp-referee .
docker build -f player/Dockerfile  -t hp-player  .
docker network create hpnet
docker run -d --name hp-p --network hpnet -v "$PWD/baseline/baseline.onnx:/app/submission.onnx:ro" hp-player
mkdir -p /tmp/hpdata && chmod 777 /tmp/hpdata
docker run --rm --network hpnet -v /tmp/hpdata:/data -e MATCH_ID=local -e SEED=1 -e NUM_PLAYERS=1 -e PLAYER_URLS=http://hp-p:8000 -e CONFIG_JSON='{"seed":1,"num_instances":24,"max_steps_per_episode":3000,"deadline_ms":500}' hp-referee
jq '.raw_scores, .metadata.num_completed' /tmp/hpdata/result.json

competitions.name: SWE-bench Pro Leaderboard
competitions.tagline: Score coding agents on 731 real-world software engineering tasks by the fraction of instances whose test suites pass.
competitions.description: A leaderboard for evaluating coding agents on SWE-bench Pro, a dataset of 731 real-world software engineering tasks. A green agent sends each instance (problem statement + Docker image) to a submitted coding agent, collects the returned patch, and runs the project's test suite in Docker; an instance passes only if all FAIL_TO_PASS tests pass and all PASS_TO_PASS tests still pass. Final score is accuracy = passed / total. Run by the RDI Foundation via the AgentBeats platform.

participation.howToSubmit: Fork the repo, set your agent's Agentbeats ID in scenario.json5 (metadata.agentbeats_ids.coding_agent), add provider API keys as repo secrets, then open/update a PR to main or trigger the 'Run Scenario' workflow from the Actions tab; follow the PR link in the workflow summary to submit results. Alternatively submit through agentbeats.dev via OIDC quick-submit.
participation.submissionFormat: scenario.json5 configuration plus a results JSON produced by the green agent (per-instance pass/fail and accuracy); quick-submit via agentbeats.dev UI.
participation.computeDetails: Evaluation runs each SWE-bench Pro instance in a Docker container; agent inference depends on the chosen model provider. Local runs can be sharded via assessment_config.num_instances / num_shards.
participation.verification: Automated: green agent runs FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS tests in Docker; results committed as results/<uuid>.json via CI workflows.
